sentences.text: For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to herein as per their status before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 01.05.2017, at about 8.15 a.m., one Somashekaraiah while crossing 1st main road,
near Ganesh Temple, Dollars Colony, Bengaluru, met with an accident with a Scooter bearing registration No.KA-04-JK- 471, because of which the said Somashekaraiah expired.

The accident happened due to rash and negligent driving of the Scooter,
which was duly insured with respondent no.1/Insurance Company.

The Tribunal has awarded a compensation of Rs.4,40,000/- along with interest at the NC:
2023:KHC:29417 rate of 8% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit of the award amount.
Not satisfied by the same, the petitioners, who are wife and children of the deceased, have preferred this appeal.
During the pendency of the appeal, appellant no.1/petitioner no.1, who was the wife of the deceased, also died and the appeal has been continued by the other petitioners.
4. The accident occurred in the year 2017.
The petitioners have not established the income of the deceased before the Tribunal.

Hence, it is deemed appropriate to fix his income notionally as per the chart prepared by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority in consultation with Insurance Companies which will be Rs.11,000/- per month.
The deceased was aged 66 years at the time of the accident.
Hence, a multiplier of 5 is adopted as per the law laid down by the Apex Court in Sarla Verma v. D.T.C [(2009)6 SCC 121].

With regard to dependency, petitioner no.1 who was the wife of the deceased and to an extent, petitioner no.4 who is a NC: 2023:KHC:29417 handicapped son of the deceased alone can be considered as dependents.
Petitioners nos.2 and 3, based on the evidence rendered cannot be considered as dependents.
Under the peculiar facts and circumstances of the case, it is deemed appropriate to deduct 1/3rd of the income of the deceased towards his personal expenses.

Thus, on the count of loss of dependency, petitioners are entitled to a sum of Rs.4,40,000/- (Rs.11,000/- X 12 X 5 X 2/3).
5.
Petitioners are also entitled to a sum of Rs.30,000/- towards 'loss of estate and funeral expenses'.

6. Petitioners are also entitled to a sum of Rs.40,000/- each towards 'loss of consortium' and thus together are entitled to Rs.1,60,000/- under this head.
7. Petitioner no.1 having died, the other petitioners being her sole legal representatives become entitled for the entire compensation.

Further, taking into consideration that petitioner no.4 is a handicapped person and was dependent on the income of his father, it is deemed NC:
2023:KHC:29417 appropriate to award him 50% of the compensation amount and petitioner nos.2 and 3 are awarded 25% each of the compensation amount.
8.
Thus, the petitioners are together entitled to an enhanced compensation of Rs.1,90,000/- over and above what has been awarded by the Tribunal (Rs.6,30,000/- minus Rs.4,40,000/-).

Further,
given the bank rate of interest, I deem it appropriate to award interest at the rate of 6% p.a. on the Siddagangambika @ Siddagangambike vs The Reliance General Ins. Co Ltd on 18 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/13605548/
